subject: Evidence playbook & control mapping — ISO/FedRAMP questions
messages:
From: Samantha Holt <samantha.holt@acme-pharma.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ZypherCloud Security <security@zyphercloud.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: compliance roadmap & evidence for ISO/FedRAMP scoping

Marcus / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Acme's procurement and security teams are starting scoping for a FedRAMP Moderate procurement (we're the SaaS procurement lead). Before we schedule a formal workshop, could you share a short roadmap and a set of sample artifacts that help us map Redwood's controls to: SOC 2 (Type II), SIG/CAIQ, and ISO 27001?

Specific asks to help with our scoping:
- Do you have a current SOC 2 Type II report or summary we can review (redacted is fine)?
- A SIG / CAIQ control mapping matrix or an index of controls you can share.
- A service boundary / data flow diagram that shows where customer data is stored, how it crosses trust boundaries, and what is run in VPC vs Redwood-hosted.
- High-level answers to: encryption at rest (KMS managed?), key rotation policy, and log retention windows for non-prod vs prod.

Also: is Redwood planning an ISO 27001 certification effort in the next 12 months, or do you have an ISO gap analysis we can look at? Any timeline for FedRAMP readiness work would be helpful.

If you prefer, we can hold a 30-min working session next week — happy to share our baseline scope (Moderate baseline).

Thanks,
Samantha Holt
Head of IT Procurement, Acme Pharmaceuticals
Samantha.holt@acme-pharma.com

--
Note: we will likely require a signed attestation or assessment engagement for the final procurement pack.
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Holt <samantha.holt@acme-pharma.com>

Subject: Re: Request: compliance roadmap & evidence for ISO/FedRAMP scoping

Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Looping in our compliance and security leads (Mina, Karthik, Neha) to respond with artifacts and timelines.

Quick plan from our side:
- Mina will attach the current redacted SOC 2 Type II summary and a SIG/CAIQ mapping (spreadsheet).
- Karthik will confirm the service boundary diagram and provide KMS/logging details (we use customer-dedicated KMS where requested; default uses managed keys).
- Neha will confirm whether an ISO 27001 certification is on our roadmap and provide the draft gap analysis if available.

We can do a 30-min working session next Wed 14 Jun or Thu 15 Jun. What works for you? I can set a meeting and include a brief agenda: scope baseline (you share Moderate must-haves), artifact review, and timelines for evidence delivery.

Action items:
- Mina: attach SOC2 + SIG mapping (by EOD today).
- Karthik: service boundary diagram and KMS notes (by Mon).
- Neha: ISO status and gap analysis (by Tue).

Best,
Marcus Lin

marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2026 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: compliance roadmap & evidence for ISO/FedRAMP scoping

Marcus / Samantha — attaching a set of initial artifacts (redacted) for your review. See the stubbed attachments below. I also included inline answers to Samantha's quick questions.

Attachments (stubs included in thread metadata):
- SOC2_Type2_2024_redacted.pdf (stub) — redacted auditor cover letter and TL;DR of control exceptions (none in prod).
- SIG-CAIQ-mapping_v1.xlsx (stub) — mapping sheet that aligns Redwood controls to CAIQ questions and SIG framework entries.
- service_boundary_diagram_v2.pdf (stub) — simplified service boundary and data flow (prod vs VPC).

Inline answers (summary):
- Encryption at rest: Customer data in hosted mode is encrypted with AES-256; we use a managed KMS (CloudKMS) by default. For Dedicated/Private we offer customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) with rotation policies configurable by customers.
- Key rotation: Default rotation 90 days for platform keys; customer-managed keys follow the customer's KMS policy.
- Logging & retention: Prod logs retained 365 days (security logs), application telemetry 90 days by default. Non-prod: 30 days unless customer requests extension.
- ISO 27001: We completed a preliminary gap analysis earlier this year; we plan to scope a formal cert effort in Q4 2026 if funding and audit slots align. I attached the draft ISO_gap_analysis_draft.docx (stub) with major control gaps flagged.

Open questions for Acme to confirm:
1) Will Acme require FedRAMP Moderate baseline covering both hosted and dedicated modes, or only hosted deployment?
2) Any vendor attestations or additional encryption/key-handling language you need in the contract?

If you want, I can walk through the SIG mapping on the call and highlight where we have full control coverage vs compensating controls.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai

Thanks Mina — helpful. A couple of clarifications ahead of our call:
- Acme requires FedRAMP Moderate coverage for the hosted offering we plan to buy (we do not need Dedicated in this procurement, although we will want the option later). Please assume Moderate baseline only.
- We will need a signed attestation that the SOC 2 report excerpts are accurate and a point-of-contact for an auditor to request limited evidence during our assessment. Can you confirm Redwood will accept a 3rd-party auditor outreach?
- Encryption detail: we need confirmation that platform-managed KMS uses tenant isolation keys (i.e., keys are not shared across tenants) or a description of how customer data is segregated cryptographically.
- Log retention: 365 days for security logs is acceptable. Please confirm log integrity controls (WORM or equivalent) and whether logs are exported to customer-specified sinks (we prefer an option to ship to our Splunk instance).

Also included: DocuSign link for a standard NDA/attestation request (we will sign once we receive the redacted SOC).

Samantha

Samantha / Marcus — quick answers and next steps from security: (copying Neha for ISO roadmap details)

1) FedRAMP Moderate scope: confirmed for hosted only. We will provide a scoped control matrix aligning our hosted architecture to the Moderate baseline.

2) Auditor outreach: Redwood accepts controlled, auditor-issued evidence requests. We will set up an evidence window and a single technical POC for auditor queries (we recommend scheduling during business hours; our TAT is typically 3 business days for targeted evidence pulls).

3) Encryption / key isolation: Hosted mode uses tenant-scoped envelope keys. Platform KMS issues a per-tenant envelope key that wraps data keys; root KMS keys are managed per-region by Redwood. For Dedicated/Private customers we support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) with dedicated keys. Detailed KMS architecture doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-evidence (linked).

4) Log integrity & export:
- Integrity: security logs are write-once, tamper-evident within our storage tier (WORM-like retention + signed checksums).
- Export: yes — we support exporting logs to customer sinks (S3, Splunk HTTP Event Collector). We can provide an export integration guide.

5) ISO status / timeline (Neha to confirm): we have a draft gap analysis targeting scoping work Q3 and formal remediation Q4 2026. Final certification in H1 2027 is optimistic but possible if audit slots are available.

Next steps:
- Marcus: schedule Wed 16 Jun 11:00 AM PT working session (will include Mina/Karthik/Neha).
- Mina: prepare SIG/CAIQ walkthrough and highlight any compensating controls.
- Neha: share ISO gap analysis highlights on the call.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
